items.title: A Late Essay
items.text:
Ms. Duarte: Come in, Wen. I saw your name on the late list again.
Wen: Yes. I wanted to explain before you said anything.
Ms. Duarte: I am listening.
Wen: The essay is almost done. But my grandmother stayed with us all week, and the only quiet room is the one I share with my brother.
Ms. Duarte: I see. And last month's assignment?
Wen: That one was honestly my fault. I forgot. I am sorry. I did not want to invent another reason.
Ms. Duarte: Thank you for telling the truth. That counts for more than you might think.
Wen: So could I have until Friday? I promise it will be good.
Ms. Duarte: Friday, then. But I am not offering a third chance. Plan your evenings, and ask me for help before the deadline, not after.
Wen: Should I send you an outline tonight so you can check my direction?
Ms. Duarte: That would be sensible. Send it by eight, and I will reply before breakfast.
Wen: Thank you, Ms. Duarte. You will have the essay on time.

qs.q: How would you describe Ms. Duarte's attitude toward Wen?
qs.why: 솔직함을 인정하며 기한을 주지만 'third chance'는 없다고 선을 그어요. 이해심 있지만 단호한 태도예요.

qs.q: Why does Ms. Duarte say, "I am not offering a third chance"?
qs.why: 금요일까지 연장을 허락하면서 다음에는 봐주지 않겠다는 경고를 하는 거예요.
o: To refuse Wen's request for an extension
To warn Wen that the teacher's patience has a limit
To suggest that Wen should drop the course
To praise Wen for working so hard

qs.q: How does Wen most likely feel during the conversation?
qs.why: 먼저 설명하겠다고 나서고 사과하며 기한을 부탁하는 모습에서 불안하지만 기대를 거는 마음이 보여요.

qs.q: In the dialogue, "counts for more than you might think" means that
qs.why: 솔직히 말하는 것이 생각보다 훨씬 가치 있다는 뜻의 표현이에요.
o: the truth will lower Wen's grade
Wen has many late assignments to count
honesty is more valuable than Wen expects

qs.q: According to Wen, why was the essay late this week?
qs.why: 할머니가 한 주 내내 머물러 조용한 방이 형제와 같이 쓰는 방뿐이었다고 했어요.
o: Wen lost the notes for the essay
A visiting relative left no quiet place to work
Wen was ill for most of the week

items.title: A Brand-New Bike
items.text:
Kai: Behold. Eleven gears, a carbon frame, and a bell that sounds like a tiny cathedral.
Sunny: Wow. You have been waving this bike at me for three days.
Kai: Because it is the best purchase of my life. Feel how light it is.
Sunny: It is light. So is your wallet now, I assume.
Kai: Money well spent. I will be at the lake in twenty minutes, while you are still waiting for the bus.
Sunny: Sure. Last time you said that, you went home pushing the bike because of a flat tire.
Kai: That was the old bike. Completely different.
Sunny: Is it? Is the rider also different?
Kai: The rider is a legend, thank you very much.
Sunny: A legend who remembers to carry a pump, I hope.
Kai: Ha, ha. Fine. Come with me on Saturday and test it yourself.
Sunny: Now that is an offer I cannot refuse. Okay, I am in.

qs.q: Which word best describes Sunny's attitude in most of the conversation?
qs.why: 자전거 자랑에 농담으로 받아치는 장난스러운 태도예요.

qs.q: Why does Sunny say, "So is your wallet now"?
qs.why: 자전거가 가볍다는 말에 지갑도 가벼워졌겠다며 비싸게 샀음을 농담으로 말한 거예요.
o: To complain that the bike is too heavy to carry up the stairs
To joke that the bike must have been expensive
To ask Kai to lend some money
To praise Kai for saving carefully

qs.q: How does Kai most likely feel when Sunny mentions the flat tire?
qs.why: 'That was the old bike. Completely different.'라고 둘러대다 웃으며 인정하는 모습에서 멋쩍지만 유쾌한 반응임을 알 수 있어요.
o: Deeply offended and unwilling to speak to Sunny again

qs.q: In the dialogue, "waving this bike at me" means
qs.why: 자전거를 흔들었다는 건 비유로, 사흘 내내 자꾸 자랑했다는 뜻이에요.
o: swinging the bike in the air

qs.q: What happened the last time Kai promised to reach the lake quickly?
qs.why: 'you went home pushing the bike because of a flat tire'라고 했어요.
o: Kai got lost on the way
Kai had to push the bike home
Kai left the bike at the lake

items.title: Cancelled at Platform Four
items.text:
Traveler: Excuse me, my train to Dalen was cancelled and the board says nothing. I have been standing here for forty minutes.
Clerk: I am so sorry for the wait. There was a signal fault north of the city, and every service is running behind.
Traveler: But nobody announced it. People are guessing.
Clerk: You are right, and I will pass that on. The announcement system is down, which is why I am walking along the queue myself.
Traveler: I have an interview at two.
Clerk: Then let us see what we can do. There is a replacement bus leaving from Gate C at 12:20. It is slower, but it will get you to Dalen by one thirty.
Traveler: That is cutting it close.
Clerk: It is, but it is the only option that does not depend on the signals. Shall I stamp your ticket for the bus?
Traveler: Yes, please. Thank you for being straight with me.
Clerk: Of course. Good luck at your interview.

qs.q: Which phrase best describes the clerk's attitude?
qs.why: 사과하고 사정을 설명하며 대체 버스를 구체적으로 제안해요. 공감하면서 실용적인 태도예요.
o: Defensive, unhelpful and quick to blame others

qs.q: Why is the clerk walking along the queue?
qs.why: 'The announcement system is down, which is why I am walking along the queue myself'라고 했어요.
o: To inform people because the announcements are not working
To check that everyone in the line has bought a valid ticket for the right train
To sell tickets for the replacement bus
To keep the passengers from entering the platform

qs.q: What does the traveler appreciate about the clerk?
qs.why: 'Thank you for being straight with me'는 완벽하지 않아도 솔직하게 말해 준 점을 고마워한다는 뜻이에요.
o: The clerk is honest, even though the news is not ideal
The clerk promises that the cancelled train will leave again within the hour
The clerk offers a refund immediately
The clerk agrees that the station is badly managed

qs.q: In the dialogue, "cutting it close" means
qs.why: cut it close는 시간 여유가 거의 없다는 관용 표현이에요. 1시 30분 도착, 2시 면접이라는 상황과 맞아요.

qs.q: According to the clerk, why is the replacement bus the best choice?
qs.why: 'the only option that does not depend on the signals'라고 했어요.
o: It is faster than the train
It stops directly at the interview
It is the cheapest way to travel
It does not rely on the signals

items.title: The Green Jacket
items.text:
Ina: Before you say anything, I need you to sit down.
Jun: That sentence never ends well. What happened?
Ina: Your green jacket. The one you lent me for the trip.
Jun: The one Mom bought me for my birthday?
Ina: There is a small stain on the sleeve. Well, maybe not small. It is the size of a coin. Maybe a large coin.
Jun: Ina.
Ina: I tried to wash it in the sink, and it just spread. I am so sorry. I will pay for the cleaning, or for a new one if it comes to that.
Jun: Let me see it. Okay. That is ink, and it is faded, not destroyed. The shop near the station can fix this.
Ina: You are not angry?
Jun: I am a little angry. Mostly I am relieved you told me instead of hanging it back in the closet.
Ina: I thought about hanging it back in the closet.
Jun: I know. That is why I am relieved.

qs.q: Which phrase best describes Ina's manner at the beginning?
qs.why: 앉으라고 말하고 얼룩 크기를 계속 줄여 말하는 모습에서 불안하고 미안해하는 태도가 보여요.

qs.q: Why does Jun say, "That sentence never ends well"?
qs.why: 'Before you say anything...'로 시작하면 나쁜 소식인 경우가 많다는 걸 농담처럼 말하며 걱정을 드러내요.
o: To ask Ina to speak more quietly
To show worry in a wry way

qs.q: What does Ina's last line suggest?
qs.why: 옷장에 도로 걸어 둘까 생각했다는 말은 숨기고 싶은 유혹이 있었다는 고백이에요.
o: She plans to buy a new closet
She wants to borrow the jacket again
She was tempted to hide the stain

qs.q: In the dialogue, "if it comes to that" means
qs.why: if it comes to that은 상황이 그렇게까지 되면이라는 뜻이에요.

qs.q: What did Ina do first about the stain?
qs.why: 'I tried to wash it in the sink, and it just spread'라고 했어요.
o: She took it to the shop near the station
She hid it in the closet
She tried to wash it in the sink
She asked their mother for advice

items.title: Faint Praise
items.text:
Dana: Did you read the report I sent you? The one on the new filing system?
Owen: I did. It was very thorough.
Dana: Thorough. Anything else?
Owen: The font was easy to read. And the charts had nice colors.
Dana: Owen, you have spent two minutes praising the colors. Did you find the content weak?
Owen: I would not say weak. I would say it left out the budget, which is what the director will ask about first.
Dana: Oh. I assumed the budget team would cover that.
Owen: They might. But if the director opens the folder and sees no numbers, she will think we did not do our homework.
Dana: I see. So the colors were your way of being polite.
Owen: Sort of. I should have started with the budget, I suppose. Can I help you add a page tomorrow morning?
Dana: Yes, please. And next time, just say it straight.

qs.q: What is Owen's attitude when he first answers about the report?
qs.why: 내용 대신 글꼴과 색만 칭찬하며 돌려 말해요. 요령 있게 피하는 태도예요.
o: Evasive but trying to be tactful

qs.q: Why does Dana say, "Thorough. Anything else?"
qs.why: 한 단어 칭찬이 부족하다고 느껴 되묻는 말이므로 더 솔직한 평가를 원한다는 신호예요.
o: To thank Owen warmly for all the praise he gave
To ask Owen to read the report again
To signal she wants more honest feedback

qs.q: How does Dana most likely feel at the end?
qs.why: 예산 누락을 깨닫고 도움을 받아들이며 다음엔 직설적으로 말해 달라고 하므로 민망하지만 고마워하는 거예요.

qs.q: In the dialogue, "did not do our homework" means
qs.why: do one's homework는 충분히 준비하다라는 뜻의 관용 표현이에요.
o: did not use the new system

qs.q: What was missing from the report?
qs.why: Owen이 'it left out the budget'이라고 말했어요.
o: The summary of the filing system

items.title: Call With Grandpa
items.text:
Grandpa: There he is! My famous grandson, with a face like a ghost.
Min: Grandpa, it is the lighting. I am in the library.
Grandpa: Fine, fine. So tell me everything. Did you pass the physics test?
Min: I did. Eighty-eight.
Grandpa: Eighty-eight! You hear that, house? Eighty-eight! Let me tell you, I never passed physics. I fell asleep in the second row.
Min: Is that so? You told me you were top of the class.
Grandpa: Top of the class at sleeping, yes. Well. You have been away at the dormitory for three months now, and the garden looks a bit empty without you pulling weeds.
Min: I will come home in December. I promise.
Grandpa: December is a good month. I will put the heater in your room early. Now go, go, you have studying to do. Eat something green.
Min: I will, Grandpa. Love you.
Grandpa: Me too. Now hang up quickly, before I say something silly.

qs.q: Which pair of words best describes Grandpa's tone?
qs.why: 손주를 반기며 농담하고 자랑스러워하는 다정하고 장난스러운 어조예요.

qs.q: Why does Grandpa mention that the garden looks empty?
qs.why: 정원이 비어 보인다는 말은 Min이 그립다는 마음을 돌려 말한 거예요.
o: To ask Min to buy plants
To hint that he misses Min

qs.q: What does Grandpa's last sentence suggest?
qs.why: 'before I say something silly'는 감정이 북받쳐 바보 같은 말을 할 것 같아 서둘러 끊자는 뜻이에요.
o: He is angry that the call has lasted so long
He is close to becoming emotional
He has forgotten what to say
He wants to continue the lecture

qs.q: In the dialogue, Min's "Is that so?" expresses
qs.why: Is that so?는 의외라는 놀람과 약간의 의심을 담은 반응이에요. 할아버지가 우등생이라고 했던 말과 달랐기 때문이에요.

qs.q: Where is Min during the call?
qs.why: Min이 'I am in the library'라고 말했어요.

items.title: Marbles at Eleven
items.text:
Mr. Okoro: Good evening. Sorry to knock so late. I am from the apartment below.
Lena: Oh, hello. Is there a problem?
Mr. Okoro: Not a problem exactly. It is just that, around eleven, I hear something rolling across the floor. Like marbles.
Lena: Marbles? Ah. That would be my cat. She has a ball with a bell inside, and she goes wild at night.
Mr. Okoro: I see. I did suspect an animal. It is only that I start work at five, and I have had trouble sleeping this week.
Lena: I am so sorry, I had no idea it carried. I can put the ball away before ten, and I will put a rug in the hallway.
Mr. Okoro: That would be very kind. Truly, I do not want to cause trouble. I like having a neighbor who waters the plants on the stairs.
Lena: Those are actually my mother's plants, but I will take the credit.
Mr. Okoro: Then thank your mother for me.

qs.q: How would you describe Mr. Okoro's way of raising the problem?
qs.why: 'Sorry to knock so late', 'Not a problem exactly'처럼 조심스럽고 공손하게 말해요.

qs.q: Why does Mr. Okoro mention the plants on the stairs?
qs.why: 불만을 말한 뒤 이웃을 칭찬해 분위기를 부드럽게 만들려는 의도예요.
o: To ask Lena to move the plants away from the stairs soon
To keep the conversation friendly after a complaint
To offer to water them himself

qs.q: How does Lena most likely feel when she learns about the noise?
qs.why: 'I am so sorry, I had no idea'라며 해결책을 제안하므로 미안해하면서 협조적이에요.
o: Offended, defensive and unwilling to change

qs.q: In the dialogue, "it carried" means that the sound
qs.why: carry는 소리가 멀리 전달된다는 뜻이에요. 위층 소리가 아래층까지 들렸다는 의미예요.
o: was loud enough to wake the cat

qs.q: What is making the rolling noise?
qs.why: Lena가 고양이가 방울 든 공을 가지고 논다고 밝혔어요.
o: A cat playing with a ball

items.title: The Alto Section
items.text:
Judge: Thank you, Priya. Please take a breath whenever you are ready, and start from the beginning.
Priya: Sorry, my hands are sweating. I am ready now.
Judge: Take your time. Thank you. That was your second verse, wasn't it? You rushed the last line.
Priya: I know. I always do that when I am nervous.
Judge: Your tone is lovely, though. Warm, especially in the low notes, and your words are very clear. Have you sung with a group before?
Priya: Only in the shower. And once at my cousin's wedding, by accident.
Judge: By accident?
Priya: The microphone was on, and I forgot to stop singing.
Judge: Well, we have a strong alto section already, but we are short of voices in the middle. Would you be willing to try a few rehearsals?
Priya: Yes! Absolutely. Thank you so much for the chance.
Judge: Do not thank me yet. Our director is demanding.

qs.q: What is the judge's attitude toward Priya?
qs.why: 마지막 줄을 서두른 점은 지적하지만 음색을 칭찬하고 연습 참여를 제안해요. 친절하고 격려하면서도 솔직해요.

qs.q: Why does Priya tell the story about the wedding?
qs.why: 경험이 없음을 우스운 일화로 말하는 건 긴장을 농담으로 덮으려는 거예요.
o: To prove that she has trained as a singer for years
To cover her nervousness with humor

qs.q: What does Priya's comment, "I always do that when I am nervous," show?
qs.why: 자신의 약점을 알고 있다는 자기 인식을 보여 줘요.
o: She does not care about the audition
She blames the judge for the mistake
She is aware of her own weakness
She has sung many times in groups

qs.q: What does the judge most likely mean by "Do not thank me yet"?
qs.why: 연습이 엄격할 것이라며 가볍게 경고하는 말이에요. 합격을 취소하는 건 아니에요.
o: A refusal of Priya's request to join the choir
A promise of a high salary
A gentle warning that the work will be hard

qs.q: What kind of voices does the choir need?
qs.why: 'we are short of voices in the middle'라고 했어요. 알토는 이미 충분하다고 했어요.

items.title: On Hold for Twenty Minutes
items.text:
Agent: Thank you for calling. My name is Sam, and I am delighted to help you today!
Caller: Finally, a person. I have been listening to your music for twenty minutes.
Agent: I do apologize for the wait. How may I brighten your day?
Caller: My router blinks red and I cannot get online. I have turned it off and on twice.
Agent: Wonderful! You have already done the first step. May I ask whether the cable at the back is firmly plugged in?
Caller: It is. I checked it before I called.
Agent: Fantastic attention to detail! Next, I would like you to hold the small button on the side for ten seconds.
Caller: Do I look like someone who enjoys holding buttons? Fine. Done. The light is green.
Agent: Marvelous! Is there anything else I can help you with?
Caller: Only that you could tell your manager twenty minutes is too long.
Agent: Absolutely, I will make a note. Thank you for being a valued customer!

qs.q: Which pair of words best describes Sam's manner?
qs.why: 상황과 상관없이 'Wonderful!', 'Marvelous!'를 반복하며 변함없이 밝은 말투를 유지해요.
o: Gloomy, slow and uninterested in callers
Unfailingly upbeat, whatever the caller says

qs.q: What is the caller's attitude?
qs.why: 20분 기다린 불만과 빈정대는 질문에서 짜증 섞인 태도가 드러나요.

qs.q: Why does the caller say, "Do I look like someone who enjoys holding buttons?"
qs.why: 묻는 형태의 반어적 표현으로 단계마다 시키는 것에 짜증이 났음을 드러내요.
o: To ask for a different button on the front of the router
To show irritation at the instruction
To refuse to follow any instruction

qs.q: What can be inferred about Sam's repeated praise?
qs.why: 사소한 일에도 똑같이 과장된 칭찬을 하는 건 정해진 응대 방식임을 시사해요.
o: It shows real surprise at the caller's skill
It is probably a routine part of the job
It was meant to hide the caller's mistakes
It was written by the caller's manager

qs.q: What finally turned the router light green?
qs.why: 손님이 옆 버튼을 10초 누른 뒤 불이 초록색이 되었어요. 전원 껐다 켜기는 이미 해 본 방법이에요.
o: Unplugging the back cable and plugging it in again
Turning the router off and on twice
Holding the side button for ten seconds

items.title: Who Wrote the Conclusion
items.text:
Ari: Hi, Bo. Great to see you at last. We have been meeting since Monday.
Bo: I know, I know. Things came up. What did I miss?
Ari: Not much. Only the outline, the survey, and most of the slides, which we finished last night.
Bo: Oh wow, that is fast. Thanks, you guys are amazing.
Ari: Yes, we are. Anyway, your section was supposed to be the conclusion. Did you start?
Bo: Almost. I have the title.
Ari: The title. Excellent. I am sure the audience will be moved by the title.
Bo: Okay, that was unkind.
Ari: Was it? I have been awake since six doing the charts. I would rather be unkind than do your part, too.
Bo: Fair. I will write it tonight and send it by nine.
Ari: Nine, then. If it does not arrive, I will present the conclusion myself and leave your name off the slide.
Bo: Understood. Nine, no later.

qs.q: What is Ari's tone when talking about the title?
qs.why: 'the audience will be moved by the title'는 제목뿐인 Bo의 진척을 비꼬는 말이에요.

qs.q: Why does Ari say, "I will leave your name off the slide"?
qs.why: 9시까지 안 보내면 이름을 빼겠다는 건 마감을 어기면 생길 결과를 경고하는 거예요.
o: To thank Bo for all the help with the slides this week
To offer Bo a shorter section
To warn Bo of a consequence for missing the deadline
To ask Bo to change the title

qs.q: What can be inferred about how Ari feels about the group work?
qs.why: Ari는 아침 6시부터 차트를 만들었다고 하며 일이 고르게 나뉘지 않은 것에 지쳐 있고 화가 나 있어요.
o: Pleased and relieved that Bo has finally joined in the work
Tired and resentful about the uneven workload

qs.q: In the dialogue, "Things came up" means that
qs.why: things came up은 예상치 못한 일이 생겼다는 뜻의 흔한 변명이에요.
o: Bo had been asked to lead the group and arrange the schedule
unexpected matters prevented Bo from attending

qs.q: By what time does Bo promise to send the conclusion?
qs.why: Bo가 'send it by nine'이라고 약속했어요.

items.title: A Cast for Six Weeks
items.text:
Dr. Hale: Good morning, Mateo. How are we feeling today?
Mateo: Honestly? Terrible. I read the scan report last night and it had so many long words that I stopped reading.
Dr. Hale: Ah. Reports are written for other doctors, not for people reading them at midnight. Let me translate.
Mateo: Please.
Dr. Hale: The scan shows a small crack in the bone of your wrist. It is clean, it has not moved, and it should heal on its own with a cast.
Mateo: A cast? For how long?
Dr. Hale: About six weeks. You will be able to write with your other hand, and I would suggest a good excuse to let someone else carry your bag.
Mateo: Six weeks. I am in a band.
Dr. Hale: Guitar?
Mateo: Drums.
Dr. Hale: Then I am sorry, but I am not worried. Your drumming will be back, and sooner than you think. Your patience, I am afraid, will need exercise.

qs.q: Which pair of words best describes Dr. Hale's manner?
qs.why: 어려운 보고서를 쉽게 풀어 주고 가방 농담까지 하는 따뜻하고 차분하며 가벼운 유머가 있는 태도예요.

qs.q: Why does Mateo say, "I am in a band"?
qs.why: 6주 깁스로 드럼을 못 칠까 걱정되어 한 말이에요.
o: To brag about his talent as a drummer
To ask for a shorter treatment
To express concern about his hobby

qs.q: What does "Your patience will need exercise" imply?
qs.why: 드럼은 돌아오겠지만 참을성이 시험받을 것이라는 말은 기다림이 답답할 것임을 뜻해요.
o: Mateo must do special wrist exercises every day
Mateo will find the waiting frustrating

qs.q: In the dialogue, "Let me translate" means that Dr. Hale will
qs.why: 전문 용어로 쓰인 보고서를 쉬운 말로 풀어 설명하겠다는 비유적 표현이에요.
o: write the report in another language
ask another doctor to read it
explain the report in plain language

qs.q: What does the scan show?
qs.why: 'a small crack in the bone of your wrist. It is clean, it has not moved'라고 했어요.
o: A badly broken bone that needs surgery soon
A small crack that has not moved

items.title: Two Minutes Late
items.text:
Hye: Pay up. Two coffees, large, no sugar, and a pastry for the witnesses.
Tae: I demand a recount.
Hye: There is nothing to recount. I said it would rain by three, and look, it is three oh two.
Tae: Two minutes late, though. A technicality, and technicalities matter in a bet.
Hye: You said, "by three." I have witnesses. Several pigeons, and one very serious seagull.
Tae: Pigeons are not reliable. They take bribes.
Hye: Is that a confession? Were you offering them bread?
Tae: Fine, fine. I will buy the coffees. But in my defense, the forecast said sunny all day, and I trusted it.
Hye: And I looked at the sky, and the sky said otherwise. Sometimes it pays to look up instead of down at your phone.
Tae: Now you are insufferable. You will remind me of this until winter.
Hye: Insufferable and caffeinated. Come on, it is pouring. I know a place with a roof, a fireplace, and cake.

qs.q: How would you describe the tone of the conversation?
qs.why: 내기를 두고 서로 농담하며 주고받는 가벼운 장난이에요.

qs.q: Why does Tae say, "Pigeons are not reliable. They take bribes"?
qs.why: 비둘기 증인을 말도 안 되는 이유로 깎아내리는 건 내기를 피하려는 익살스러운 변명이에요.
o: To report a real crime to the police
To find a funny excuse for not paying

qs.q: How does Tae really feel when saying "Now you are insufferable"?
qs.why: 곧바로 커피를 사겠다고 하고 웃어넘기는 장면에서 진짜 화난 게 아니라 재미있어하는 걸 알 수 있어요.
o: Deeply offended and ready to leave

qs.q: In the dialogue, "insufferable" means
qs.why: insufferable은 참을 수 없을 만큼 거슬린다는 뜻이에요. 이긴 Hye가 으스대는 걸 농담으로 말한 거예요.

qs.q: What did Hye predict?
qs.why: Hye는 'I said it would rain by three'라고 했어요.

items.title: Eyes on the Road
items.text:
Dad: Mirror, signal, then check over your shoulder. Good. Now ease off the brake, slowly, and let the car roll.
Seo: My hands are slippery on the wheel, and my heart is racing. Is that normal?
Dad: Completely. Mine were the same on my first lesson, and my instructor sat there with a thermos and never blinked.
Seo: Did you hit anything?
Dad: A mailbox. A very small mailbox. The mailbox forgave me.
Seo: That is not helping.
Dad: It was supposed to help. Let us try something else. Forget the other cars. Just look at the road far ahead, where you want to go.
Seo: Okay. It is easier. It is smoother, too.
Dad: Right. Your eyes steer the car; your hands only follow. You are doing well, Seo. Slow and steady, and breathe.
Seo: Can I take the next turn? I think I can manage it.
Dad: Gladly. Signal first, and check your mirror again.

qs.q: Which pair of words best describes Dad's attitude?
qs.why: 긴장한 아이에게 농담과 구체적 조언으로 차분하게 안심시켜요.

qs.q: Why does Dad tell the story about the mailbox?
qs.why: 자신도 초보 때 실수했다고 말해 Seo의 긴장을 풀어 주려는 의도예요.
o: To warn Seo about the dangers of the road ahead
To comfort Seo by showing he also made mistakes
To explain why he sold his car

qs.q: What does Seo's final question suggest?
qs.why: 다음 커브를 해 보겠다는 말은 자신감이 붙고 있다는 신호예요.
o: Seo wants to stop the lesson

qs.q: In the dialogue, "ease off the brake" means
qs.why: ease off는 힘을 서서히 푼다는 뜻이에요.

qs.q: According to Dad, what steers the car?
qs.why: 'Your eyes steer the car; your hands only follow'라고 했어요.
o: How hard you hold the wheel

items.title: Forgiveness Week
items.text:
Student: Hi. I need to return this, and I would like to know about the fine. I am afraid it is rather large.
Librarian: Let me scan it. Hmm. Forty-two days overdue. That comes to twenty-one dollars.
Student: Twenty-one dollars. For one novel. I could have bought it new.
Librarian: You could have. But then you would have missed the pleasure of paying for it three times.
Student: Is that supposed to be a joke?
Librarian: A small one. Here is the thing: the library has a Forgiveness Week this month. Anyone returning a long-overdue book can read to the children on Saturday morning instead of paying.
Student: Read aloud? To children? I would be terrible.
Librarian: Everybody says that. Then twelve small faces look up at them, and suddenly they are brilliant.
Student: Hmm. What time on Saturday?
Librarian: Ten. Shall I put your name down?
Student: Yes. But if the children throw books at me, I am blaming you.
Librarian: Noted.

qs.q: Which description best fits the librarian's manner?
qs.why: 농담을 곁들이지만 벌금 대신 읽기 활동이라는 해결책을 알려 줘요. 건조한 유머와 친절이 섞여 있어요.

qs.q: Why does the librarian mention Forgiveness Week?
qs.why: 연체료를 내는 대신 어린이 책 읽어 주기를 할 수 있다고 알려 주려는 거예요.
o: To announce that the library is closing for the month
To offer the student a way to avoid the fine
To ask the student to buy a new copy
To warn the student about more fines

qs.q: How does the student feel at the start of the conversation?
qs.why: 'I am afraid it is rather large'에서 민망해하고 21달러에 낙담한 모습이에요.

qs.q: What does the student's last joke suggest?
qs.why: 책을 던지면 탓하겠다는 농담은 긴장되지만 하기로 했다는 의미예요.
o: The student is refusing to take part in the event
The student agrees, though a little nervous
The student wants to pay the fine

qs.q: What time will the children's reading take place?
qs.why: 'on Saturday morning'이고 시간은 'Ten'이라고 했어요.
o: Noon on Saturday, after the library closes

items.title: Flour and Early Light
items.text: At four in the morning the bakery on Alder Lane is the warmest room in the neighborhood. Marisol rolls her sleeves above her elbows and slides the first trays into the ovens, humming a tune she can never name. Outside, the street lamps still glow orange, and nobody has yet walked past the window. Inside, the air is thick with butter and yeast, and the radio murmurs a weather report to no one. She does not mind the hour. Years ago she dreaded alarm clocks; now she thinks of these dark, unhurried hours as her own private secret. By six, the first customers will arrive, stamping their boots and complaining about the cold, and the quiet will break into cheerful noise. But for now there is only the soft thud of dough on the table, the slow rising of golden loaves, and a contentment so complete that she would not trade it for any office or any view.

qs.q: Which phrase best describes the atmosphere in the bakery before six o'clock?
qs.why: 빵집 안은 '가장 따뜻한 방'이고 조용하며 만족감이 가득해요. 아늑하고 평화로운 분위기예요.

qs.q: What is the writer's main purpose in this passage?
qs.why: 글쓴이는 이른 새벽 일에서 느끼는 조용한 만족감을 묘사해요. 제빵 과정 설명이나 광고가 아니에요.
o: To explain step by step how bread is baked in a large bakery
To persuade readers to start waking up earlier
To convey the quiet satisfaction of an early-morning job
To advertise a bakery to people in the area

qs.q: What can be inferred about Marisol's attitude toward her working hours?
qs.why: 'Years ago she dreaded alarm clocks; now ... her own private secret'에서 예전엔 싫어했지만 지금은 소중히 여긴다는 걸 알 수 있어요.
o: She tolerates them only until she changes jobs
She still resents them but hides it from customers
She would prefer to work in a busier place
She has come to treasure them

qs.q: In the passage, "unhurried" most nearly means
qs.why: unhurried는 서두르지 않고 여유 있는 상태예요. 문맥상 방해받지 않는 조용한 시간을 뜻해요.
o: calm, with no pressure to rush
so short that they pass unnoticed

qs.q: What does Marisol do while she works?
qs.why: 'humming a tune she can never name'에서 이름을 모르는 곡을 흥얼거린다고 했어요.
o: She sings along with the radio
She hums a tune she cannot name
She reads the weather report aloud
She talks quietly to the first customers

items.title: Declining the Offer
items.text: Subject: Re: Offer of Employment. Dear Mr. Castillo, Thank you for the generous offer to join your design team, and for the kindness you showed me during every stage of the interview. I have spent the past three days weighing my decision, and it has not been easy. Your studio does exactly the kind of work I hoped to do when I first picked up a pencil. However, I have also been offered a position at a small workshop in my hometown, where I would be able to care for my father while he recovers from surgery. After much thought, I have decided to accept that role and must therefore decline yours. Please do not mistake my answer for a lack of interest; I admire your team enormously, and I would be honored to be considered again should another opening arise in the future. Thank you again for your time and trust. With sincere regards, Haru Ogawa

qs.q: Which word best describes the tone of the email?
qs.why: 감사와 존중을 표현하면서 거절하는 것을 아쉬워하는 어조예요. 정중하고 아쉬워하는 태도가 드러나요.

qs.q: Why did Haru write this email?
qs.why: 'must therefore decline yours'로 거절하면서도 'would be honored to be considered again'으로 좋은 관계를 유지하려 해요.
o: To ask for a higher salary and better hours before accepting
To refuse a job while keeping a good relationship
To request details about the design team
To complain about the way the interview was run

qs.q: What can be inferred about the main reason for Haru's decision?
qs.why: 스튜디오 일은 원하던 일이라고 했고, 아버지를 돌보기 위해 고향 일자리를 택했으므로 가족 사정이 이유예요.
o: The studio's work did not match Haru's artistic interests or goals
The salary offered was lower than expected
Family responsibilities outweighed the career opportunity
Haru lacked confidence in the design skills

qs.q: In the email, "weighing my decision" most nearly means
qs.why: weigh는 여기서 장단점을 신중히 따져 본다는 뜻이에요. 사흘 동안 고민했다는 맥락이에요.
o: delaying the answer on purpose to gain an advantage
measuring the cost of the offer

qs.q: What does "that role" refer to?
qs.why: 'that role'은 바로 앞 문장의 'a position at a small workshop in my hometown'을 가리켜요.
o: The design team leader's position at the studio
The job of caring for a recovering patient in a hospital
A future opening that might arise at the studio
The position at the workshop in Haru's hometown

items.title: Accepting the Trophy
items.text: Thank you, thank you, please sit down; my knees are shaking harder than yours. When our coach told us in September that we would finish last in the league, I remember thinking that was generous. We had one working ball, a field that flooded whenever it drizzled, and a goalkeeper who was afraid of the ball. (That is you, Tomas, and I say it with love.) Yet here we are, holding this trophy, which, I notice, is lighter than I expected and heavier than I deserve. I should confess that I did not score the winning goal. I did not even touch the ball in the final. I stood at midfield shouting advice that nobody followed. This victory belongs to the seventeen people who ran when they were tired, laughed when they lost, and turned up on rainy Tuesdays. So tonight, please do not clap for me. Clap for the flooded field, for the single ball, and for Tomas, who, I am told, saved four penalties last week. I am still in shock.

qs.q: Which pair of words best describes the tone of the speech?
qs.why: 농담을 섞으면서 자신의 공을 낮추고 있어요. 유머러스하고 겸손한 어조예요.

qs.q: Why does the speaker say, "please do not clap for me"?
qs.why: 승리는 'the seventeen people' 팀원 모두의 것이라고 말하며 자신에게 박수 치지 말라고 해요. 공을 팀에게 돌리려는 의도예요.
o: To give the credit to the whole team
To avoid being interrupted by noise
To show disappointment with the audience
To end the speech as quickly as possible

qs.q: What does the phrase "that was generous" suggest about the team before the season?
qs.why: 꼴찌를 할 거라는 코치의 예상이 '관대한' 것이라고 생각했다는 건 팀이 매우 약해 보였다는 뜻이에요.
o: The coach had praised every player equally
The team had plenty of money for equipment
The league was known for easy opponents
Few people expected it to do well

qs.q: In the passage, "turned up" most nearly means
qs.why: turned up은 여기서 '(모임에) 나타나다, 오다'라는 뜻이에요. 비 오는 화요일에도 연습에 왔다는 맥락이에요.

qs.q: What problem did the practice field have?
qs.why: 'a field that flooded whenever it drizzled'에서 가랑비에도 물에 잠겼다고 했어요.
o: It was too small for a full match
It had been closed for repairs in September
It flooded when light rain fell
It was covered with uneven grass

items.title: Review: Midnight Orchard
items.text: I wanted to love Midnight Orchard, a card game in which two to four players race to harvest apples before dusk falls. The box is beautiful: the illustrations glow, the cards feel thick and smooth, and the wooden apple tokens are a delight to hold. For the first twenty minutes, my friends and I were enchanted. Then the rules began to fray. A card that lets you "swap any two orchards" turned out to contradict the instruction on the next page, and we spent a quarter of an hour arguing over the booklet instead of playing. Even when we agreed, the game dragged; one round took almost an hour, and by the end the winner seemed less thrilled than relieved. Would I recommend it? To collectors who prize handsome objects, perhaps. To anyone who simply wants a pleasant evening, I would suggest a lighter game, and perhaps a better-edited rulebook. I will keep the box, though. It looks lovely on the shelf.

qs.q: Which description best fits the reviewer's overall attitude?
qs.why: 겉모습은 칭찬하지만 규칙과 진행에는 실망했어요. 실망했지만 디자인은 높이 평가하는 태도예요.
o: Furious and completely unforgiving toward the makers
Confused and unable to form an opinion
Disappointed, though still appreciative of the design

qs.q: What is the main purpose of the review?
qs.why: 장점과 단점을 모두 평가하고 'Would I recommend it?'라며 누구에게 맞는지 말해요. 구매 판단을 돕는 글이에요.
o: To teach readers how to play the game from the beginning, step by step
To help readers decide whether the game is worth buying
To compare it with the previous version
To invite readers to a game night

qs.q: What does the reviewer imply by "I will keep the box, though"?
qs.why: 상자가 선반 위에서 예쁘다는 말은 게임 자체보다 외관이 매력이라는 뜻을 담아요.
o: The reviewer plans to play it again soon
The reviewer wants to return it to the shop
The game's appeal is mostly in how it looks
The game will be improved in a later edition

qs.q: In the passage, "fray" most nearly means
qs.why: fray는 천이 올이 풀리듯 무너지기 시작한다는 뜻이에요. 규칙이 모순을 일으키며 허물어졌다는 맥락이에요.

qs.q: What caused the long argument during play?
qs.why: 'swap any two orchards' 카드가 다음 쪽의 지시와 모순되었다고 했어요.
o: One player was caught cheating during the second round
A card was missing from the box
Two instructions in the rulebook disagreed
The apple tokens were hard to count

items.title: Notice to Residents of Cedar Court
items.text: We regret to inform you that electricity to all apartments will be switched off on Thursday, 12 June, from 9:00 a.m. to approximately 3:00 p.m. The interruption is necessary so that engineers can replace an aging cable that has caused three brief blackouts since the winter. We understand that this is inconvenient, particularly for those working from home, and we apologize sincerely for the short notice, which was caused by a delay in receiving the necessary parts. Elevators will not operate during this period; residents who need help with stairs should call the management office by Wednesday noon, when volunteers will be arranged. Please unplug sensitive equipment before leaving, and remember that food in refrigerators will stay cold for several hours if the doors remain closed. A free hot lunch will be served in the community room from noon. Thank you for your patience and cooperation. We are confident that this work will prevent far greater disruption later. The Management Office

qs.q: Which word best describes the tone of the notice?
qs.why: 불편을 사과하면서도 대책(점심, 도우미)을 안내하며 안심시켜요. 사과하되 안심시키는 어조예요.

qs.q: What is the main purpose of the notice?
qs.why: 정전 일정과 이유, 대비 방법을 알리는 공지예요. 점심은 보조 정보일 뿐이에요.
o: To announce a planned power cut and explain how to prepare
To report that a cable has been stolen from the basement room
To ask residents to pay for repairs
To invite residents to a community lunch

qs.q: What can be inferred about the management's view of the work?
qs.why: 마지막 문장에서 이 공사가 더 큰 문제를 막아 줄 것이라고 확신해요. 불가피하고 가치 있다고 보는 거예요.
o: They think it is unnecessary but required by law
They are unsure whether it will solve anything
They see it as unavoidable and worthwhile
They regard it as a minor matter for residents

qs.q: In the notice, "interruption" most nearly means
qs.why: interruption은 여기서 전기 공급이 일시적으로 끊기는 것을 뜻해요.
o: a rude comment during a talk
a change of the building's owner
a long-term plan for the future

qs.q: By when should residents who need help on the stairs call the office?
qs.why: 'call the management office by Wednesday noon'이라고 명시했어요.

items.title: Gate 14, Midnight
items.text: By midnight, Gate 14 looked like the aftermath of a small, sleepy battle. Coats were piled on seats, a toddler lay across two suitcases, and a man in a suit had given up on dignity entirely and was snoring beneath a vending machine. The board above us had announced our flight as "delayed" at seven, "delayed further" at nine, and, with what I took to be sarcasm, "delayed" once more at eleven. At first I had complained loudly. Then I had complained quietly. Now I simply watched the clock, which seemed to be moving backward. Across the aisle, a woman about my grandmother's age pulled a deck of cards from her bag and asked if anyone knew how to play rummy. Within ten minutes, six strangers were arguing cheerfully over the rules. Somebody shared a bag of peanuts. Somebody else shared a charger. When the announcement finally came at one o'clock, I was almost sorry to hear it, since I was in the middle of a winning hand.

qs.q: Which phrase best describes the narrator's tone?
qs.why: 지친 상황을 농담처럼 묘사하고 마지막엔 오히려 아쉬워해요. 재치 있게 웃어넘기는 어조예요.

qs.q: Why does the narrator mention the man snoring beneath a vending machine?
qs.why: 품위를 포기한 채 자판기 아래서 자는 모습으로 승객들의 지친 상태를 익살스럽게 보여 줘요.
o: To complain about the airport's lack of seats and comfortable chairs
To show humorously how worn out the travelers were
To warn readers about rude passengers
To explain why the flight was delayed

qs.q: How did the narrator's feelings change over the night?
qs.why: 처음엔 크게 불평했지만 카드놀이 후엔 안내 방송이 나오자 'almost sorry'였어요. 짜증에서 뜻밖의 즐거움으로 변했어요.
o: From excitement about the trip to disappointment

qs.q: In the passage, "aftermath" most nearly means
qs.why: aftermath는 어떤 일이 지나간 뒤의 상태예요. 게이트가 전투가 끝난 뒤처럼 어수선했다는 비유예요.
o: the beginning of a long journey by plane
the scene left after something has happened

qs.q: What did the woman across the aisle ask?
qs.why: 'asked if anyone knew how to play rummy'라고 했어요.
o: Whether someone could lend a charger
Whether the flight had been canceled
Whether anyone knew how to play rummy

items.title: The Violin in the Attic
items.text: The attic smelled of cedar and forgotten summers. Pia had come up only to find a winter blanket, but her flashlight caught a long black case behind a roll of carpet, and she stopped breathing for a moment. The latches opened with a reluctant click. Inside, resting on faded blue velvet, lay a violin whose varnish had darkened to the color of tea. A single string was missing. Pia lifted it carefully, as one lifts a sleeping bird, and noticed a name scratched inside the body in tiny letters: Elio, 1961. Nobody in her family had ever mentioned an Elio, or a violin. Downstairs, a door slammed and the house resumed its ordinary noises, but up here time seemed to be holding its breath. She turned the instrument over once more, then closed the case gently, as if the thing might wake. She still needed the blanket. But she knew, with a certainty that surprised her, that she would be back tomorrow with questions.

qs.q: Which word best describes the mood of the passage?
qs.why: 오래된 다락방, 이름 모를 바이올린, 숨죽인 시간이 신비로운 분위기를 만들어요.

qs.q: Why does the writer compare lifting the violin to lifting "a sleeping bird"?
qs.why: 잠든 새를 들듯이라는 비유는 조심스럽고 부드러운 손길을 강조해요.
o: To suggest that the violin is alive and breathing
To explain that the violin is very heavy
To hint that Pia is afraid of animals
To show how gently and carefully Pia handles it

qs.q: What can be inferred about Pia's family?
qs.why: 가족 중 누구도 Elio나 바이올린을 언급한 적이 없다고 했어요. 그녀가 몰랐던 가족사가 있을 수 있어요.
o: They have always talked openly about the violin's history
There may be a family history she knew nothing about
They have lived in the house only a short time

qs.q: In the passage, "reluctant" most nearly means
qs.why: reluctant click은 마치 열기 싫다는 듯 뻑뻑하게 열리는 소리예요. 마지못한 듯한 느낌을 줘요.

qs.q: Why did Pia go to the attic in the first place?
qs.why: 'had come up only to find a winter blanket'이라고 했어요.
o: To search for her family's old photographs
To look for a missing string

items.title: Bring Back the Handwritten Note
items.text: Last week I received a birthday card with a message written in blue ink, slightly smudged, in my aunt's looping handwriting. It took me two minutes to read and about two seconds to realize I had not held something so personal in years. We send thousands of messages a day, yet most vanish the moment they are answered. A text can be quick, clever, even kind, but it arrives dressed in the same plain font as a delivery notice. A handwritten note, by contrast, shows effort: someone chose the paper, spent a few careful sentences, and walked to a mailbox. Critics will say that I am being sentimental, and perhaps they are right. Nevertheless, I challenge every reader to write one real letter this month, to a friend, a relative, or a teacher who once believed in you. It need not be long. Mistakes are welcome. What matters is that the recipient will be able to keep it in a drawer, and to take it out on a gray afternoon when no screen can offer the same comfort.

qs.q: Which pair of words best describes the tone of the passage?
qs.why: 개인적인 경험으로 시작해 독자에게 편지를 쓰라고 따뜻하게 설득해요.

qs.q: What is the writer's main purpose?
qs.why: 'I challenge every reader to write one real letter this month'에서 손편지를 쓰도록 권하는 글임을 알 수 있어요.
o: To describe how greeting cards are manufactured
To encourage readers to write a letter by hand
To criticize people who send text messages

qs.q: What does the writer suggest by comparing a text to "a delivery notice"?
qs.why: 문자가 배송 안내문과 같은 평범한 글꼴로 온다는 말은 개성 없고 사무적으로 보인다는 뜻이에요.
o: Texts are more expensive than letters

qs.q: In the passage, "sentimental" most nearly means
qs.why: sentimental은 실용성보다 정서에 이끌린다는 뜻이에요. 글쓴이가 감상적이라는 비판을 예상한 문맥이에요.
o: guided by tender feelings more than practical thinking
fond of spending money on expensive gifts and cards

qs.q: In the sentence "It need not be long," what does "It" refer to?
qs.why: It은 바로 앞에서 쓰라고 한 'one real letter'를 가리켜요.
o: The letter each reader is asked to write
The birthday card that the aunt sent last week

items.title: Before You Fly
items.text: My dearest Nari, By the time you read this, you will be somewhere over the ocean with a window seat and too many snacks, I hope. I wanted to put a few thoughts on paper because I am not good at speeches, and because I know I will talk about the weather at the airport instead of what I mean. So here is what I mean. I am not worried that you will fail. I am only a little worried that you will forget to eat properly, and so I have packed three jars of my plum jam, which you must ration like treasure. When the language feels like a wall, remember that every wall has a door; you simply have not found the handle yet. When you are homesick, which you will be, look at the moon. It is the same one that shines over this garden. And when you succeed, as I know you will, remember to celebrate with your new friends, not only with us. We will hear all about it, and we will be the proudest people in the world. All my love, Grandpa

qs.q: Which pair of words best describes the tone of the letter?
qs.why: 손주를 향한 애정이 가득하고 용기를 북돋아 줘요.

qs.q: Why did the writer decide to write a letter?
qs.why: 'I am not good at speeches ... talk about the weather at the airport instead of what I mean'에서 직접 말하기 어려워 편지를 쓴다는 걸 알 수 있어요.
o: The writer will not be able to attend the farewell at the airport
Speaking about feelings face to face is difficult for the writer
The airport would not allow long conversations
Nari asked for advice in writing

qs.q: What does the phrase "every wall has a door" suggest?
qs.why: 벽에도 문이 있다는 말은 어려워도 해결책을 찾을 수 있다는 격려예요.
o: Nari should avoid crowded places with many walls and doors
Language difficulties can be overcome with time
Nari will probably fail the language test

qs.q: In the letter, "ration" most nearly means
qs.why: ration은 아껴서 조금씩 나누어 쓴다는 뜻이에요. 잼 세 병을 보물처럼 아끼라는 말이에요.

qs.q: What does the writer tell Nari to do when homesick?
qs.why: 'When you are homesick ... look at the moon'이라고 했어요.
o: Eat a spoonful of plum jam

items.title: Me Versus the Wardrobe
items.text: According to the box, assembly would take "about forty-five minutes with two adults." I had one adult, namely me, and an enormous confidence that lasted until step three. The instructions, drawn by someone who clearly despised words, showed a cheerful cartoon figure holding a screwdriver and smiling like a person who had never been disappointed. I was not smiling. By hour two, I had discovered eleven leftover screws, none of which the diagram acknowledged. By hour three, the wardrobe leaned gently to the left, like a tired traveler, and I decided this was a design choice. My neighbor, passing in the corridor, politely asked whether everything was all right. "Perfectly," I said, from beneath a door panel. Tonight, the wardrobe stands in my bedroom. It holds my clothes. It also holds, I suspect, a grudge. If you ever see me carrying another flat box up the stairs, please do me the kindness of tripping me.

qs.q: Which pair of words best describes the tone of the passage?
qs.why: 자신의 실패를 과장해서 웃음거리로 삼는 어조예요.

qs.q: Why does the writer describe the smiling cartoon figure in the instructions?
qs.why: 행복하게 웃는 그림과 웃지 못하는 글쓴이를 대비시켜 답답함을 강조해요.
o: To praise the clarity of the drawings and diagrams in the booklet
To explain which tool is needed
To suggest that the wardrobe is cheap
To contrast its cheerfulness with the writer's frustration

qs.q: Why does the writer say, "I decided this was a design choice"?
qs.why: 기울어진 옷장을 고칠 수 없으니 일부러 그렇게 만든 것처럼 받아들이며 스스로를 위로하는 거예요.
o: To make an uncorrectable flaw seem acceptable
Because the box listed the lean as a feature
Because a neighbor praised the shape
Because the wardrobe was meant to hold heavy items

qs.q: In the passage, "acknowledged" most nearly means
qs.why: acknowledge는 존재를 인정하거나 언급한다는 뜻이에요. 도면에 그 나사가 나와 있지 않다는 맥락이에요.

qs.q: How many extra screws did the writer find?
qs.why: 'eleven leftover screws'라고 명시했어요.

items.title: Room 308
items.text: The corridor outside Room 308 was painted the soft green of hospital walls everywhere, a color chosen, Rina suspected, to calm people who were not calm at all. She had counted the ceiling tiles twice. She had read the poster about hand-washing three times. Across from her, a vending machine hummed to itself, and she had bought nothing from it because her hands refused to stop trembling. Her brother had gone in for the operation at eight; it was now almost noon. Each time a door opened, her heart lurched, and each time it was only a cleaner, a visitor, a nurse hurrying elsewhere. Finally the door of 308 swung wide, and a surgeon in a pale blue cap stepped out, pulling off her gloves. She looked tired; then she smiled. "He is awake," she said, "and he is already asking for toast." Rina laughed, and the laugh turned into something else halfway through, and for a long moment she could not speak at all.

qs.q: Which description best fits the mood of the passage?
qs.why: 긴 기다림의 불안이 의사의 소식으로 안도로 바뀌어요.

qs.q: Why does the writer mention that Rina counted the ceiling tiles twice?
qs.why: 타일을 두 번이나 세는 행동은 초조함을 달래려는 몸짓이에요.
o: To explain that the corridor was newly built
To suggest that the hospital was badly run
To show that she enjoyed counting
To show how anxious and restless she was

qs.q: What can be inferred from "the laugh turned into something else halfway through"?
qs.why: 웃음이 다른 것으로 바뀌었다는 건 감정이 북받쳐 울음이 터졌다는 뜻이에요. 좋은 소식을 들은 직후라 안도감 때문이에요.
o: Rina became angry at the surgeon
Rina was suddenly embarrassed by the joke
Rina was overwhelmed and began to cry
Rina suspected bad news was coming

qs.q: In the passage, "lurched" most nearly means
qs.why: lurch는 갑작스럽게 휘청하며 움직이는 거예요. 문이 열릴 때마다 가슴이 철렁했다는 뜻이에요.

qs.q: Why had Rina bought nothing from the vending machine?
qs.why: 'she had bought nothing from it because her hands refused to stop trembling'이라고 했어요.
o: It was out of order and showed an error message
Her hands would not stop trembling
She had no money with her
A nurse had told her not to eat

items.title: Inside the Glassworks
items.text: Gather round, everyone, and please keep behind the yellow line; the furnace you can feel on your faces is hotter than a summer in the desert, and I would like all of you to leave with your eyebrows. Isn't it marvelous? Look at Mr. Brandt's hands as he turns the pipe. He has done this for thirty-one years, and still he treats every bubble of molten glass as if it were the first. Watch how he blows, just gently, and the orange blob swells like a sunrise in his palm. Notice that he never hurries. Glass cannot be rushed; it punishes impatience with cracks. Now, I am told that some of you were hoping to try this yourselves. I am afraid that is a privilege reserved for people with a decade of training and a very steady nerve. However, in the shop at the end of the tour, you may hold finished pieces, admire the colors, and, if your wallet permits, take one home. Shall we move on? Mind the step; it is steeper than it looks.

qs.q: Which pair of words best describes the guide's manner?
qs.why: 작업을 감탄하며 소개하고 눈썹 농담을 하는 열정적이고 유머러스한 태도예요.

qs.q: Why does the guide say, "I would like all of you to leave with your eyebrows"?
qs.why: 화로가 매우 뜨거우니 노란 선 뒤에 머물라는 경고를 농담으로 표현한 거예요.
o: To suggest that the visitors dress more warmly on their next visit
To complain about the heat in the building
To warn visitors to keep a safe distance in a humorous way
To announce that the furnace is broken

qs.q: What does the guide's description of Mr. Brandt suggest about the guide's feeling toward him?
qs.why: 31년째 매번 처음처럼 정성을 다하는 모습을 감탄하며 소개하므로 존경심이 드러나요.
o: Jealousy of his long and successful career
Worry that he works too slowly
Deep respect for his patient skill
Surprise that he is so young

qs.q: In the passage, "privilege" most nearly means
qs.why: privilege는 소수에게 허락된 특권이에요. 오랜 훈련을 받은 사람만 직접 해 볼 수 있다는 맥락이에요.
o: a heavy duty that everyone must perform each day
a cheap item sold in a shop
a special right given to only a few people

qs.q: Where may visitors hold finished glass pieces?
qs.why: 'in the shop at the end of the tour, you may hold finished pieces'라고 했어요.
o: In the shop at the end of the tour
At the start of the tour

items.title: The Word I Missed
items.text: The word was "rhythm." I know it now as I know my own name, but standing under the stage lights, with the judge's pen hovering, my mind turned white and empty like a freshly washed page. I spelled it r-y-t-h and heard the bell. It rang so softly and so finally. I walked off the stage with my face burning, smiling at nobody. For a week afterward I avoided the dictionary the way people avoid a former friend. Then, on a rainy Thursday, my teacher handed me an envelope. Inside was a card signed by every student in the class, and on the front, in huge, wobbly letters, was the word "RHYTHM," spelled perfectly. I laughed so hard I had to sit down. It occurs to me now that the bell did not take anything from me except a trophy I had not yet earned. What I kept was the memory of being laughed with, rather than at, and a spelling I will never again forget.

qs.q: Which pair of words best describes the tone of the passage?
qs.why: 실패를 되돌아보며 따뜻하게 웃어넘기는 어조예요.

qs.q: What is the writer's main purpose?
qs.why: 대회에서 틀린 창피한 일이 반 친구들의 카드 덕분에 좋은 기억이 된 이야기예요.
o: To explain the rules of a spelling contest to new participants
To blame the judge for an unfair decision
To advise readers to study the dictionary
To show how an embarrassing failure became a pleasant memory

qs.q: What can be inferred about the narrator right after leaving the stage?
qs.why: 'face burning, smiling at nobody'와 사전을 피한 모습에서 창피하고 위축된 상태를 알 수 있어요.
o: The narrator felt embarrassed and withdrawn
The narrator felt proud of the effort
The narrator was angry at the classmates
The narrator looked forward to the next round

qs.q: In the passage, "hovering" most nearly means
qs.why: hover는 한 곳 위에 머물러 떠 있다는 뜻이에요. 심사위원의 펜이 멈칫 머물러 있는 모습이에요.
o: staying in the air near one spot

qs.q: What was written on the front of the card?
qs.why: 카드 앞면에 'in huge, wobbly letters'로 철자가 맞는 'RHYTHM'이 적혀 있었어요.
o: The word spelled correctly in large letters
The signatures of all the judges from the contest
A message of thanks to the teacher

items.title: Concerning the Shared Courtyard
items.text: Dear Members of the Residents' Committee, I am writing, once again, about the bicycles in the shared courtyard. As I mentioned in my letters of March and June, the area beside the main entrance has gradually become a storage space for at least a dozen bicycles, two scooters, and what I believe is a broken stroller. I do not wish to appear unreasonable. I understand that our building lacks a proper bicycle room, and I appreciate that many neighbors depend on their bikes for work. Nonetheless, last Friday my elderly neighbor, carrying shopping, had to step into the road to reach the door. I would be grateful if the committee would, at its next meeting, consider installing racks along the east wall and setting a clear date by which loose items must be removed. I remain, as ever, willing to help with the cost or the labor. Yet I confess that my patience, though considerable, is not without limit. I look forward to your reply and trust that it will not take another three months. Yours faithfully, A. Mensah

qs.q: Which pair of words best describes the tone of the letter?
qs.why: 정중한 표현을 쓰지만 인내에 한계가 있다고 분명히 말해요.

qs.q: Why does the writer say, "I do not wish to appear unreasonable"?
qs.why: 불평을 하기 전에 자신이 억지를 부리지 않는 사람임을 먼저 밝히려는 거예요.
o: To show fairness before making a complaint
To apologize for writing the letter
To admit that the complaint is unimportant

qs.q: What can be inferred from "I trust that it will not take another three months"?
qs.why: 'another three months'라는 표현은 이전에도 답이 늦었다는 걸 암시해요.
o: The committee meets only once a year
Earlier letters received very slow answers
The writer will soon move away
The committee has already agreed to the racks

qs.q: In the letter, "considerable" most nearly means
qs.why: considerable은 상당한, 꽤 큰이라는 뜻이에요. 인내심이 상당하지만 무한하지는 않다는 맥락이에요.

qs.q: Why did the elderly neighbor step into the road last Friday?
qs.why: 마당이 자전거로 막혀 있어 짐을 든 이웃이 문까지 가려고 도로로 내려갔어요.
o: The neighbor was riding a scooter
The east wall was being repaired
The bicycles blocked the way to the door
The neighbor wanted to avoid a stroller on the stairs
